title: Invited: Conformal Inference meets Evidential Learning: Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification with Epistemic and Aleatoric Separability
problem: Uncertainty quantification in deep learning models deployed at the edge faces computational constraints, requiring models to assess confidence while operating on resource-limited devices.
motivation: Reliable uncertainty estimation enables safer AI applications in critical domains by allowing models to recognize when predictions lack knowledge.
method: Conformalized Evidential Quantile Regression (CEQR) works by combining two techniques: conformal inference (which provides statistical guarantees without assuming the data follows any particular distribution) and evidential learning (which trains models to estimate their own uncertainty). It separates two sources of uncertainty: epistemic uncertainty (what the model doesn't know and could learn with more data) from aleatoric uncertainty (randomness built into the data itself that can't be eliminated). Because conformal inference doesn't require distributional assumptions, the system maintains statistical guarantees while running fast enough on resource-constrained devices like phones and IoT sensors.
key_novelty: CEQR's core innovation is merging conformal inference and evidential learning to provide uncertainty estimates with statistical guarantees (without distributional assumptions) that separately distinguish model uncertainty from data uncertainty, all while running efficiently on edge devices.
contributions: Lightweight framework (CEQR) combining conformal inference and evidential learning
Distribution-free statistical guarantees without distributional assumptions
Efficient separation of epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties
Real-time applicability on resource-limited edge devices

metrics.other: statistical robustness and real-time edge deployability

limitations: Specific experimental results, computational overhead, and comparison with baselines not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Distribution-free uncertainty quantification for edge-deployed AI
